svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.9.8.4 Location of Exits
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.9 MEANS OF EGRESS
Location of Exits

text.tspan: path of travel between the exits

g.text: Remote: an exit at each end of the corridor
Not remote: one fire can make both exits unusable

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Where more than one exit is required from a
floor area, at least 2 exits are independent
of each other and placed remote from each
other along the path of travel between them
The intent
If one exit is made untenable or inaccessible by
a fire, or its exterior door is blocked by an
exterior incident, another exit is available.
Exits close together might all be made untenable
or inaccessible by the same fire.
How far apart
As far apart as possible, with the Part 3
criteria as a target. Article 3.4.2.3. generally
requires the distance between exits to be one
half the diagonal dimension of the floor area or
at least 9 m (29′-6⅜″). Designs with exits so
close together that both will obviously be
contaminated in a fire are not acceptable.
Drawn: the same corridor with two exit layouts, walls cut low. Gold: corridor. Pink: exit stairs.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.9.8.4. (page 9-53), with Note A-9.9.8.4.(1).
